chapter.title: Tanning or Dyeing Extracts; Tannins and Their Derivatives; Dyes, Pigments and Other Coloring Matter; Paints and Varnishes; Putty and Other Mastics; Inks

page.h1: HTS Chapter 32: Tanning or Dyeing Extracts; Tannins and Their Derivatives; Dyes, Pigments and Other Coloring Matter; Paints and Varnishes; Putty and Other Mastics; Inks — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Paint, Pigments & Ink by Country (HTS Ch. 32) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, Mexico, the EU, China, Korea, Japan, Brazil, India, Taiwan and the UK charge on U.S. paint, titanium dioxide, dyes, caulk and printing ink.
keywords: does mexico have tariffs on us goods

intro: U.S. paint, pigments, caulk and ink enter **duty-free in the three biggest markets**: Canada and Mexico charge nothing on goods that qualify for USMCA, and the **EU** has charged nothing on any U.S. Chapter 32 good since July 1, 2026 (it charged up to 6.5% before). South Korea is also free under KORUS. **China** is the expensive market: its MFN rate of 5%–10%, its 2019 counter-tariffs of 5%–25% plus 2.5%, and the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods take U.S. solvent-based paint to 42.5% and titanium dioxide pigment to 29% unless the Chinese buyer holds an exclusion. Brazil charges up to 14%, India 7.5%–10%, and Japan, Taiwan and the UK 0%–6.5%. Beyond the tariff, what decides access for paints and inks is chemical and product rules: REACH, CLP and the VOC limits of Directive 2004/42/EC in the EU, Canada's VOC limits for architectural coatings, Mexico's paint-labelling standard, and chemical registration in Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada ($2.34B, 30% of the chapter, down 0.2%) is the largest buyer, mostly of paints (3209, $613M; 3208, $590M) and caulks (3214, $391M). Qualifying goods enter free, and neither of Canada's counter-tariff lists has a Chapter 32 item; architectural paints must meet Canada's VOC limits.
profile.mainProducts: Water-based paints & varnishes (3209) · Solvent-based paints & varnishes (3208)

regulator.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (VOC limits for architectural coatings) and Health Canada (surface coating materials)
regulator.requirement: An architectural coating may not be manufactured, imported or sold in Canada if its VOC concentration exceeds the limit for its category in the Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) Concentration Limits for Architectural Coatings Regulations (SOR/2009-264); dilution instructions must be in English and French. Lead and mercury in surface coatings are limited by the Surface Coating Materials Regulations (SOR/2016-193)

Since July 1, 2026 every Chapter 32 line enters free from the U.S., against up to 6.5% before; REACH registration and the paints VOC directive still decide what can be sold.
profile.mainProducts: Titanium dioxide & other pigments (3206) · Synthetic organic dyes & pigments (3204)

regulator.name: European Chemicals Agency and national authorities (REACH, CLP, paints VOC Directive 2004/42/EC)
regulator.requirement: Substances in a paint, pigment or ink imported at 1 tonne a year or more must be registered under REACH (Regulation (EC) 1907/2006) by the EU importer or an only representative, mixtures must be classified and labelled under CLP (Regulation (EC) 1272/2008), and decorative paints and vehicle refinishing products must meet the VOC limits and labelling of Directive 2004/42/EC

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for 2023 (the latest year WITS holds for these markets) for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading: 3206.11 for titanium dioxide pigments, 3208.90 and 3209.10 for paints, 3214.10 for caulks and mastics and 3215.19 for color printing inks. National 8–10-digit lines can differ, and where a subheading has several national lines the basis gives their range.
Taiwan's cells use the applied MFN rates of January 30, 2026 printed for each national line in the AIT-TECRO Agreement on Reciprocal Trade schedule, instead of WITS.
USMCA (Mexico, Canada) and KORUS (South Korea) give 0% to U.S. goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows each market's MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.

For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 lists all of Chapter 32 in Annex I and sets 0% on U.S.-origin goods from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, on proof of non-preferential U.S. origin; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then. The Commission can suspend the cut.

China's cells add, in order, China's MFN rate, the counter-tariff the line carries under Announcement No. 3 of 2019 (25%, 20%, 10% or 5%), 2.5% from the September 2019 list (Announcement No. 4 of 2019, halved from February 14, 2020; 5% on writing ink 3215.9010), and the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods. An importer with an exclusion pays only the MFN rate plus 10%.
India's rates are the basic customs duty only; surcharges and IGST are not included. Brazil, Japan and the UK show MFN rates; none has a trade agreement that cuts these rates for U.S. goods.
